An endless sea of golden sunset cloud stretching to the curved horizon far below, the sun a molten disc, the cloud-tops gilded amber and rose.
A sky dotted with other distant floating isles drifting in the haze, each a tiny silhouette, the cloud-sea rolling away beneath them all.
A rippling green-and-violet aurora draped across the night sky behind the castle, stars scattered above the dark cloud-sea below.
A clear cobalt sky pierced by towering thunderheads climbing miles upward, their white anvil crowns blazing in full sun, the cloud-sea churning darkly far beneath.
A misty dawn breaking over the cloud-sea, pale gold light bleeding into lavender and grey, the castle's shadow stretching long and blue across the luminous fog below.
A star-strewn twilight cradling an enormous moon so close its craters are visible, the cloud-sea below shimmering silver in its cold, overwhelming light.
A savage storm churning far below, lightning flickering silently through the dark mass, the castle riding above it in serene stillness, the abyss gaping between.
God-rays pouring through a cathedral of cloud, each shaft of light miles wide, the cloud-sea below ignited in columns of gold and blinding white.
A blood-red sunset bleeding across the horizon, the cloud-sea stained deep crimson and violet, the sky above fading to bruised purple where the first stars emerge.
A serene high-altitude blue so pure and thin it borders on black at the zenith, the distant cloud-sea a white floor impossibly far below, the world a memory.
A vast nebula smeared across the night sky, rose and teal and burning amber, its reflected glow softly illuminating the cloud-sea in faint unearthly colours below.
A thick blanket of pewter cloud pressing close below the castle, hiding the world entirely, only cold grey sky above and the muffled rumble of hidden thunder beneath.
A double rainbow arching fully across the eastern sky after rain, its colours impossibly vivid, the cloud-sea below still wet and gleaming under returning gold light.
A bone-white blizzard raging at the cloud-sea level far below, the castle above it in frozen clarity, a sky of hard diamond stars and absolute arctic silence.
A sky layered in horizontal bands of colour at sunset, cobalt above shading to jade, then saffron, then deep magenta at the cloud horizon, the depth vertiginous.
A thin crescent moon hanging low near the horizon, Venus burning beside it, the cloud-sea a black velvet plain below, the silence of deep space pressing close overhead.
A scorching midday sky bleached pale at the zenith, the sun a ferocious white point, the cloud-sea below flattened and glittering like hammered tin under the merciless glare.
A sky haunted by vast dark shapes moving beneath the cloud-sea, their shadows rolling across the white surface, their nature unknown, the scale of them filling the horizon.
An autumn twilight of deep amber and rust, ragged clouds backlit in burning orange, the cloud-sea below the colour of old embers slowly cooling toward the dark.
A tropical sky stacked with towering cumulus palaces glowing pink and white in the late afternoon, the cloud-sea below lush and soft, the air warm even at this height.
A sky during a solar eclipse, the sun a black disc ringed in white fire, the cloud-sea below plunged into sudden violet twilight, stars appearing in broad daylight.
A vast curtain of virga hanging from high cloud, rain evaporating before it ever reaches the cloud-sea, the sky painted in translucent grey veils drifting in slow silence.
A pre-storm greenish sky, the light sickly and strange, the cloud-sea below heaving and darkening, a wall of weather fifty miles wide advancing across it with terrible patience.
A frozen winter dawn, the cloud-sea below a motionless white plain, the sky above flushed the faintest rose on one edge, everything else still deep cold blue-black.
A sky so thick with distant stars at altitude that the Milky Way casts a faint shadow, the cloud-sea below a dark mirror reflecting their ancient scattered light.
